output_text: {"regions":[{"label":"Figure 6.7","kind":"chart","bbox":[0.084,0.476,0.536,0.906],"summary":"Radar chart comparing adoption of four legal and regulatory enablers for sharing private-intent data across four country income groups; adoption is generally low, with a marked exception for digital ID verification/authentication among high-income countries.","details":"Title: “Adoption of enablers for sharing private intent data lags those for public intent data across country income groups.” Four radar axes: Data portability right for individuals (top); Data portability formatting requirement (right); Private sector able to digitally verify or authenticate ID (bottom); and Mandate for voluntary licensing of access to essential data on FRAND basis (left). The radial scale is marked 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100 percent. Legend: High-income (blue), Upper-middle-income (green), Lower-middle-income (orange), Low-income (purple). The plotted groups are clustered at relatively low levels on the portability and FRAND-licensing axes. On the digital ID verification/authentication axis, the high-income series extends substantially farther than the others; the other groups also extend farther on this axis than on most of the remaining axes. Source: WDR 2021 team, based on World Bank, Global Data Regulation Survey. Note: Percent of countries in each income group that had adopted good-practice legal and regulatory frameworks to enable access to, sharing, and reuse of private-intent data as of 2020.
